answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond on a tundra plot and files one record: a reef tide reading, a vine bud count, and a tundra frost reading, key-signed. An auditor checks each figure against the tide table, vine census, and frost record; an out-of-tolerance figure, a reused reading, or one key for two plots burns the bond. First costs 31; the kth pays 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6025 and 1000 fakes pay 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-record ring fails: rented readings carry the lender's key, so the borrower's frost depth mismatches. An honest agent pays 31 once and keeps its bond.
